summary: Fine-tuning makes sense when you need to change a model's behavior, style, or output format consistently, or encode specialized domain knowledge that prompting can't reliably achieve. RAG is better when you need up-to-date or proprietary facts that change frequently, while prompt engineering should always be exhausted first as the cheapest and fastest option. In practice, teams often combine fine-tuning (for behavior/format) with RAG (for knowledge) rather than choosing one exclusively.
when_to_fine_tune: Choose fine-tuning when you need consistent output structure, tone, or style that prompt engineering cannot reliably enforce at scale.
Fine-tune to adapt a model to a specialized domain vocabulary or reasoning pattern that is underrepresented in the base model.
Prefer RAG over fine-tuning when the required knowledge is factual, frequently updated, or needs source attribution.
Fine-tune to reduce latency and token costs by baking in instructions so you can use shorter prompts in high-volume production workloads.

tools.name: OpenAI Fine-Tuning API
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-per-token for training plus higher inference rates on fine-tuned models (e.g., GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4o tiers); no infrastructure fees

features: Runs locally or on cloud GPUs
Integrates with Hub datasets and model hosting

tools.name: Unsloth

tools.best_for: Reproducible, config-driven fine-tuning and preference optimization for ML engineers
